passage: The Lindqvist group investigated turnover of c-Myc, a regulatory protein that is rapidly degraded in proliferating cells. To measure stability without confounding new synthesis, cells were treated with cycloheximide, an inhibitor of translation elongation, and harvested at the times shown. Lysates were resolved by SDS-PAGE, transferred to a membrane, and probed with an antibody against c-Myc; band intensities were quantified and normalized to a loading control. Degradation of c-Myc was assumed to follow first-order kinetics. The researchers hoped to compare half-lives under normal and stressed conditions and to learn whether proteasome inhibition would stabilize the protein. Results from unstressed cells are shown; each value is the mean of three biological replicates, with errors below 5% of the mean. Equal total protein was loaded in every lane, as confirmed by the loading control. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What fraction of c-Myc remains 120 minutes after cycloheximide treatment?
questions.explanation: At 120 min, two half-lives have elapsed (100 → 50 → 25%).
questions.trap: Choosing 12.5% (three half-lives) or 50% (one half-life) rather than the value at 120 min; two half-lives have elapsed there.

questions.stem: Why is cycloheximide used in this experiment?

options.A: It accelerates proteasomal degradation of all proteins
options.B: It increases transcription of the gene
options.C: It blocks new synthesis so that the loss of existing protein can be followed
options.D: It labels the protein for detection by antibody

questions.explanation: Without blocking translation, newly synthesized protein would obscure the decay of the pre-existing pool.
questions.trap: Thinking cycloheximide accelerates degradation or raises transcription rather than stopping new synthesis so only the decay of the pre-existing pool is observed.

questions.stem: If the decay continues to be first-order, what percentage of c-Myc remains after 300 minutes?
questions.trap: Miscounting half-lives: 4 half-lives gives 6.25% and 6 gives 1.562%, while 300 / 60 = 5 half-lives gives 3.125%; 96.875% is the amount lost, not remaining.

questions.stem: Which statement about first-order decay is INCORRECT?

options.A: The half-life is independent of starting concentration
options.B: The rate of decay is proportional to the amount remaining
options.C: The half-life equals ln 2 divided by the rate constant
options.D: The half-life increases as the starting amount of protein increases

questions.explanation: In first-order kinetics, t½ = ln 2/k and does not depend on starting concentration.
questions.trap: Accepting that the half-life increases with starting amount as true, confusing first-order decay with kinetics where half-life depends on concentration.

questions.stem: c-Myc turnover is typically controlled by which system?

options.A: Glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus that prevents degradation
options.B: Ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome
options.C: Phosphorylation by glycolytic kinases that leads to secretion

questions.explanation: Polyubiquitin chains (K48-linked) mark proteins for proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibitors such as MG132 stabilize short-lived regulatory proteins.
questions.trap: Choosing lysosomal, Golgi glycosylation or secretion routes, none of which explains the short half-life of c-Myc; the ubiquitin-proteasome system does.
